page: Google Cloud Platform m2-megamem-416 is a high-capacity instance in the Memory Optimized family, engineered for workloads requiring vast physical address space. Powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 208 physical cores and 416 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware vector support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The system is equipped with 5,888 GB (5.75 TB) of RAM, yielding 14.15 GB of memory per core. The server includes no local storage and zero hardware GPUs, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput alongside modest per-core metrics. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 363,157.31, complemented by top-tier PassMark CPU (101,498.44) and encryption (158,258.46) results. The memory subsystem maintains high transfer rates, recording 20,541.48 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 684.81 GB/sec in uncached 256MB reads. Conversely, single-core throughput is constrained, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,009.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1,349.58, which limits sequential task rates such as small-model LLM generation at 13.32 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the platform consolidates massive computing footprints into a single host, lowering network coordination overhead for large shared-memory datasets. Tradeoffs include the total reliance on remote storage fabrics and limited single-thread performance compared to newer standard instances. Google Cloud Platform m2-megamem-416 is suited for ultra-large in-memory database engines such as SAP HANA, massive enterprise analytics, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m2-megamem-416 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 416 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs across 208 physical cores at 2.7 GHz and 5,888 GB of system RAM. With 14.15 GB of memory per vCPU and AVX-512 vector support, it provides massive scale for memory-bound tasks, though it includes neither local storage nor GPUs. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core computing with a stress-ng score of 363,157.31 and uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 684.81 GB/sec. However, single-threaded metrics remain modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,009.0. The instance optimizes resource density for memory footprint consolidation rather than single-thread latency. It is targeted at ultra-large in-memory databases, enterprise data warehouses, high-concurrency Clang compilation, and heavy analytic processing.
